title: INSTALL lists absent files or build outputs as distributed sources
reproduction: Resolve every FILES entry against exact Git paths and inspect configure outputs and file modes.
expected: Point to checked-in inputs and identify artifacts produced later.
observed: libpcap listed ten unresolved names/patterns including SUNOS4, two misplaced tests, net and obsolete manual names; its BPF wrapper was called a symlink and its LICENSE entry named tcpdump. tcpdump listed generated tcpdump.1.
fix: Keep the missing SunOS objects explicitly historical; remove stale entries and name the actual wrapper, tests, manual templates and README.md.
test_evidence: All 101 libpcap and 172 tcpdump final entries match exact-case tracked paths, directory prefixes or globs. configure creates net and the manuals; the regular bpf_filter.c includes bpf/net/bpf_filter.c.

title: BSD BPF is presented as the only kernel filter and a general prerequisite
reproduction: Compare the filtering summary and BPF installation advice with the Linux, BSD and packetfilter backends.
expected: Distinguish BPF filter programs from the BSD BPF device.
observed: The README claimed all non-BPF-device packets are filtered in user space; INSTALL told systems without BPF to obtain its driver.
fix: Describe the Linux socket filter and user-space fallback, and limit the old BSD driver instructions to applicable systems. Point Tru64 readers to README.tru64.
test_evidence: pcap-linux.c uses setsockopt with SO_ATTACH_FILTER; pcap-bpf.c and pcap-pf.c have BIOCSETF paths. configure.in selects linux, pf and bpf separately.

title: INSTALL misstates what the compiler and flex probes enforce
reproduction: Compare the compiler, lexer and warning text with the two generated configure scripts and libpcap/aclocal.m4.
expected: Describe the checks separately from upstream tool recommendations.
observed: Both guides promised an abort for non-ANSI compilers. libpcap implied a 2.4.6 patch-version check and misquoted its null-interface diagnostic.
fix: Describe the ISO C89 option probe, retain the historical flex recommendation, and quote the actual warning.
test_evidence: Both C89 probes report unsupported in the xno case; the libpcap flex probe checks flex -V exit status. --without-flex and --without-bison select lex and yacc. The null case emits the two uppercase WARNING messages.

title: Fork instructions point to an issue tracker
reproduction: Compare the AIX contribution destination with libpcap/README's separate source and issue destinations.
expected: Name the repository as the fork target.
observed: The URL for forking ended in /issues.
fix: Point to the upstream repository itself.
test_evidence: Compared local URL strings only. configure.in independently confirms --with-pcap=dlpi and AIX BPF detection through odmi.h; URL reachability not tested.

title: DAG and Septel instructions name libcap instead of libpcap
reproduction: Compare both step 2 instructions, the DAG success message and the bare Septel option with libpcap/configure.
expected: Identify the library and reproduce the local option handling accurately.
observed: Both steps named another library; the DAG message omitted 'the', and the Septel default did not specify the source-directory base.
fix: Name libpcap, quote the DAG probe and qualify the bare --with-septel lookup.
test_evidence: configure accepts --with-dag[=DIR], --with-septel[=DIR] and --with-pcap=TYPE; dag/septel branches define DAG_ONLY/SEPTEL_ONLY. Bare --with-septel falls back to $srcdir/../septel; the check reads INC/msg.h.

title: DAG read timeouts and batching described as unconditional
reproduction: Compare the timeout and 64 kB claims with the streams and non-streams branches in pcap-dag.c.
expected: State which read path supports a timeout and when batching applies.
observed: The text promised a timed return regardless of packets and a 64 kB minimum without the immediate-mode exception.
fix: Scope the timeout to the streams API and distinguish the normal and immediate thresholds.
test_evidence: pcap-dag.c passes maxwait to dag_set_stream_poll, uses mindata 65536 or 0 on activation, and explicitly says dag_offset does not support timeouts.

title: README promises both helpers set an exact device mode
reproduction: Read both named helpers and the launchd plist; compare the permission operations with rw-rw----.
expected: Do not imply that existing access by other users is revoked.
observed: Neither helper assigns mode 0660: both change group and add group permissions.
fix: Document chgrp admin and chmod g+rw, including the permissions they leave unchanged.
test_evidence: ChmodBPF/ChmodBPF and chmod_bpf both contain those two operations on /dev/bpf*. The plist targets /usr/local/bin/chmod_bpf. No script, launch service or permission change was run.

title: README tells readers to generate configure.in with the wrong tools
reproduction: Compare the autotools recipe and device-open description with configure.in, configure and pcap-sita.c.
expected: Use the supplied configure script and describe the implemented activation path.
observed: The recipe treated configure.in as generated output and called for automake; the open description named pcap_open().
fix: Remove the regeneration steps, retain --with-sita and describe activation without naming a nonexistent local entry point.
test_evidence: configure.in is input to autoconf; Makefile.in and configure are tracked, Makefile.am is not. The SITA option sets V_PCAP and V_FINDALLDEVS to sita. pcap_activate_sita calls acn_open_live.

title: tcpdump directs readers to retrieve libpcap unnecessarily
reproduction: Follow the claimed libpcap FTP pointer in the readme, then inspect the sibling tree and the local-library search.
expected: Identify the bundled source or an installed development package as alternatives.
observed: README.md required fetching and building libpcap; INSTALL pointed to a tcpdump README FTP location that describes tcpdump itself.
fix: Use ../libpcap and its INSTALL.txt for the source route; distinguish the standalone build from the application.
test_evidence: Sibling paths are tracked; tcpdump/configure checks for $dir/libpcap.a under ../libpcap and supports installed libraries. settings.gradle lists :app and :sentrystub, not :tcpdump.

title: Legacy trace examples mismatch the scripts' inputs and output units
reproduction: Compare the sample filenames, packet size argument, output fields and row 4 narrative with the bundled AWK sources.
expected: Use the file the example produced, set a numeric segment size and interpret the output as printed.
observed: The example used tracedata after writing tracefile and supplied the literal avgsize. It called occurrence counts duplicate counts and plotted scaled sequence numbers as raw numbers.
fix: Use tracefile and a numerical -v packetsize; identify the legacy format, per-script time origin and sequence units; interpret row 4 directly.
test_evidence: Read all four scripts: packetsize defaults in BEGIN, counters are preincremented, stime/atime divide by 1024. Row 4 has six sends and one ack: 2.00 minus 1.86 is 0.14 s. No trace or tool was used.

title: WinDump guide conflates WinPcap and libpcap and misnames local paths
reproduction: Resolve the workspace, makefile, libpcap notes and output paths relative to the archived tcpdump source.
expected: Separate external prerequisites from local project files using tracked case.
observed: The alternative download suggested libpcap alone; the indeterminate README.Win32 and windump-prefixed directories did not identify the checked-in files.
fix: Point to the sibling libpcap guide, the separate WinPcap distribution and project-relative win32/prj paths and outputs.
test_evidence: WinDump.dsw names WinDump.dsp; its /out settings are release/WinDump.exe and debug/WinDump.exe. GNUmakefile sets PCAP_DIR=../../../winpcap and links -o windump.exe. The sibling libpcap.dsp is a static-library project.

title: INSTALL extends HP-UX 11.00 patch advice to all 11.x
reproduction: Compare the scope of the outbound-support patch paragraph with README.hpux.
expected: Keep the historical 11.00 advice distinct from the 11i report.
observed: INSTALL said HP-UX 11 needs patches while the platform note explicitly exempts 11i.
fix: Limit the claim to 11.00 and refer to the original platform report for 11i.
test_evidence: README.hpux distinguishes 11.00 from 11i (11.11), including the absence of the kernel switch on 11i. No historical patch or host behavior was independently tested.
